learnings.question: Which economist, in a 1971 essay, first articulated the idea that in an information-rich world, the growth of information itself consumes a scarce resource: the attention of its recipients?
learnings.learning: Economist Herbert Simon argued in 1971 that an information-rich world creates a scarcity of attention, since information consumes the attention of whoever receives it.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: In one blogger's automated personal content-curation system, what single question does an AI model ask to decide whether to keep or discard a YouTube video from a daily feed?
options: Would a Muslim, Malaysian software engineer early in his career actually benefit from watching this?
Is this video trending in my country right now?
Does this video have more than 10,000 likes?
Is this video shorter than 20 minutes?
learnings.learning: A personal content engine filters daily YouTube videos through a single AI-asked question tailored to the curator's own identity and career stage, discarding anything that doesn't pass.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: Which 19th-century German psychologist discovered that people forget roughly 80% of newly learned material within 24 hours unless they actively work to recall it?
learnings.learning: Hermann Ebbinghaus showed in the 1880s that roughly 80% of newly learned information is forgotten within a day unless actively recalled, which is the basis for spaced repetition.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What is the name of the psychological phenomenon, also called the 'Google Effect', in which people are less likely to remember information they expect to be able to look up again later?
learnings.learning: The 'Google Effect', also known as Digital Amnesia, describes how our brains treat saving information externally as permission to forget it.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In the Scrum framework, which artifact visually tracks how much work remains in a Sprint to show whether the team is on schedule?
learnings.learning: The Burndown Chart is a Scrum artifact that visualizes a Sprint's progress by showing the work remaining over time.

learnings.question: In Agile and Scrum methodology, what is the main purpose of breaking a project into short, iterative cycles called Sprints?
options: To increase the overall length of the project
To reduce the number of team members needed
To eliminate the need for planning meetings
To allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments
learnings.learning: Scrum divides work into short Sprints specifically to make a project more flexible and able to adjust quickly, rather than to shorten teams or skip planning.

learnings.question: A common framework describing the purpose of human life in Islam centers on three primary roles. Which of the following is NOT one of those three roles?
options: Serving as a steward (khalifah) of the Earth
Living life as a test of faith and conduct
learnings.learning: A common Islamic framework describes human purpose through three roles: worship of Allah, stewardship (khalifah) of the Earth, and living life as a test of faith and conduct, rather than the pursuit of material wealth.

learnings.question: Which verse of the Quran states, 'I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me'?
learnings.learning: Quran 51:56 states that jinn and mankind were created for the purpose of worshiping Allah, forming the foundational basis of worship in Islamic theology.

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what Arabic term, referenced in Quran 2:30, refers to humanity's role as a steward or trustee placed in authority over the Earth?
learnings.learning: Khalifah is the Arabic term for humanity's role as steward or successive authority on Earth, as introduced in Quran 2:30.

learnings.question: In the PCIe (PCI Express) power management specification, which link state is the deepest power-saving mode, used for the longest periods of inactivity, with the highest power savings and the longest wake-up time?
learnings.learning: L2 is the deepest PCIe power state, used during the longest idle periods, offering the greatest power savings at the cost of the longest time to resume activity.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: What is cited as the primary motivation for implementing power management states in the PCIe (PCI Express) standard?
options: Reducing the physical size of the PCIe connector
Increasing data transfer bandwidth between devices
Improving backward compatibility with older PCI slots
Efficient use of energy, extending device longevity, and enhancing system performance
learnings.learning: PCIe power management states exist to make efficient use of energy, extend device longevity, and enhance system performance in power-sensitive environments.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what term refers to the actual, unfolding occurrence of events in a person's life, as shaped by their own actions and decisions?
learnings.learning: Qada' refers to the actual occurrence of events in one's life, which can be influenced by a person's own actions and decisions, as distinct from Qadr.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: Which Quranic verse states that 'Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves'?
learnings.learning: Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:11 teaches that Allah does not change a people's condition until they change what is within themselves, tying personal change to Qada'.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: A data analysis applying the Pareto Principle (the 80/20 rule) to the words of the Quran found that the 20 most frequently occurring words account for roughly what percentage of the entire text?
learnings.learning: Despite the Pareto Principle's 80/20 expectation, the 20 most frequent words in the Quran only account for about 20.83% of its total text.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: In Arabic script, what term refers to the small diacritical marks placed above or below letters to indicate vowel sounds and pronunciation?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are the diacritical marks added to Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds, and their absence makes reading Arabic text more ambiguous.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
